How do you give Street Performers money before their act is up?
They usually have their stuff nearby, place it there (where visible) and if possible make sure they see you.
Sometimes they have someone walking around the act through the crowd to collect money.

And they conveniently take your money from your bag without you even noticing.

Such convenience.

...Or be polite and stay: for street artists, the larger the crowd, the more people it attracts. Also, as a spectator, don't you hate when someone leaves the room in the middle of it? I know the same etiquette doesn't apply for street performances, but truly, but for your money, the best you can do for them is to be there form beginning to end. [Disclaimer: Theatre Tech speaking, yeah I do street stuff and I love it :) ]
I typically use my hands but feel free to be creative.

Former busker (street performer) here. Let me clue you in on a little secret.

We don't care about the act. We care about getting some money to eat.

I started off, when I was hitch hiking, with an acoustic guitar. I really wasn't good. I had a few songs, and that was it. When I lost my guitar jumping a train, I switched to juggling. I wasn't very good at that either. If someone stayed too long, my act would be shot. The less I could play, the better off I was.

I'm not saying there aren't great street performers. Far some it. Some great people do incredible bits. It's just that the model that makes it work is people stopping for a minute or so, giving money and moving on.

If you're curious, best I day I ever had was six hundred for two hours worth of work. The average day, however, was about forty dollars.

Seriously, all they're accomplishing is making us wait like 3 seconds on that "We're verifying you're not a botnet" page. Oh no!

Ah that's just what you see :-)

Voat uses Cloudflare as a security provider (Cloudflare and their main competitor Akamai are the worlds biggest security providers for internet traffic).

in those 3 seconds, your browser connects to Cloudflare and says hi. Cloudflare then checks if it recognizes you as a spammy source against a list it keeps, and checks the content of your greeting message for anything suspicious.

If everything turns out ok, it lets you through and you get to see the voat site. If not, it blocks your traffic and makes sure voat isn't bothered by it, giving more bandwith to real users.

This is a bit of a simplification, but that's what happens.

When voat is down because of an attack, you'll get to see a page of Cloudflare, stating voat is down/unreachable, maybe you've seen it earlier today.

So in short, those 3 seconds are crucial in case of an attack.

Hope this helped clear it up a little.
